reason: The cited evidence shows that in-flight oxidation occurs during HVOF spraying of HEA powders and influences phase composition and properties (E1, E3), but it does not demonstrate control of oxide dispersion via oxygen partial pressure, formation of nano-scale precipitates, dislocation pinning, or any effect on creep resistance. The key mechanistic premises are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: In-flight oxidation during HVOF spraying of HEA powders can be controlled by varying oxygen partial pressure.
In-flight oxidation produces oxide precipitates within the HEA matrix.
Nano-oxide precipitates can pin dislocations and retard creep deformation.
Oxide dispersion can be optimized to improve creep resistance without causing brittleness.
The HEA coating system (FCC/BCC) is amenable to oxide dispersion strengthening via thermal spray processing.
